Thanks for taking the time during last week's call. As discussed in our RFI, our architecture team needs a detailed runbook for Redwood's private (VPC / on-prem / air-gapped) deployment model so we can validate operational fit. Specifically we need:

- A deployment runbook that covers pre-install validation, networking (VPC/subnet/CIDR expectations), firewall ports, and recommended A/B upgrade paths for air-gapped clusters.

Jordan —

Thanks — we can absolutely provide those. I am attaching the initial runbook (v1.2) with the sections you called out and a one-page summary for procurement. Highlights below so your reviewers can triage quickly:

- Network: recommended 3-tier zone layout (control, workload, mgmt), required ports (6443 for k8s API, 8080/8443 for agent endpoints), and optional NAT egress for telemetry.
- Security: customer-managed KMS supported via HSM/KMS integrations (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, GCP KMS); we support envelope encryption and key rotation.
- Air-gapped installs: signed image bundle with SHA256 verification, offline package transfer, and an upgrade checklist that preserves KV cache snapshots.
- Rollback: canary upgrades + hot fallback to last known-good model binary; instructions included.

Next steps: Monica will follow up with SOC2 summary and the network diagram for import. I can schedule a short walkthrough next week if that helps.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Jordan — adding the technical supplements you requested. Attached: SOC2 control summary (redacted) and the network_zone_diagram.png you can import. Quick notes for your architects:

- KMS/HSM: For air-gapped environments we recommend customer-provided HSM for master key wrapping. Redwood's key hierarchy supports wrapping keys with an external HSM via PKCS#11. We do not retain unwrapped master keys.
- Image distribution: We sign all runtime artifacts. Offline delivery uses signed tarballs; install script performs SHA256 verification before load.
- Upgrades/patching: Offline patch bundle + preflight check (disk, available memory, kernel modules). In the runbook there's an explicit sequence for model binaries, runtime, and config so that KV cache migrations are consistent.
- Auditing: Agent forwards audit events over TLS to your collector; for air-gapped installs we support local collector dump export with signed manifests.

Attachments: SOC2-Summary-Redwood.pdf, network_zone_diagram.png

If you want, we can redact any vendor-specific references prior to inclusion in your procurement packet.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Senior Product Manager, Security Integrations — Redwood Inference
